Kaman stands {{convert|7|ft|0|in|m|abbr=on}} and played the [[Center (basketball)|center]] position. He was selected sixth overall in the first round of the [[2003 NBA draft]] by the [[Los Angeles Clippers]], after a [[college basketball]] career at [[Central Michigan University]]. ==High school and college career== Kaman attended Tri-unity Christian School in [[Wyoming, Michigan]], leading his high school varsity to the state Class D quarterfinals in 2000, before losing to Lenawee Christian School. He went on to play for three seasons at [[Central Michigan University]], leading them to a [[Mid-American Conference]] Championship and an [[National Collegiate Athletic Association|NCAA]] tournament first-round win in 2003. He then garnered [[Associated Press]] Honorable Mention All-America honors before declaring for the 2003 NBA draft, where the Clippers selected him sixth overall. Kaman claims he decided to enter the NBA draft a year early so he could fund a chicken farm in his home state of Michigan.{{cite web|url=https://deadspin.com/five-tiny-tidbits-on-the-los-angeles-clippers-203210|title=NBA Five Tiny Tidbits On: The Los Angeles Clippers|website=Deadspin.com|date=September 26, 2006}} ==Professional career== ===Los Angeles Clippers (2003–2011)=== In his rookie year, Kaman averaged 6.1 points, 5.6 rebounds, 0.89 blocks and 22.5 minutes in 82 games played (61 starts). He was the only Clipper to play all 82 games. Kaman became only the second rookie in franchise history ([[Michael Brooks (basketball)|Michael Brooks]], 1980–81) to play in all 82 games in his rookie season. He finished the season ranked second among all rookies in blocked shots per game (.89 bpg), third in field goal percentage (.460) and fourth in rebounds per game (5.6 rpg), earning the starting Center position on the NBA Rookie All-Star Team. He tallied eight points (4–7 FG) and seven rebounds in 19 minutes played, though the Rookies lost to the Sophomore team.[http://www.nba.com/history/allstar/rookie_box_2004.html 2004 Rookie Challenge: Sophs 142, Rooks 118] [[File:Chris Kaman Clippers.jpg|thumb|left|Kaman helped the Clippers to their first playoff series victory in [[2006 NBA Playoffs|2006]].]] A year after his rookie season, Chris Kaman improved his play by averaging 9.1 points, 6.7 rebounds and 25.9 minutes in 63 games (50 starts). He had missed 12 games due to injury, including the first 11 games of the season due to a left ankle sprain. Kaman continued to create milestones in his career as he scored in double-figures in 30 games and recorded four games with 20 or more points. Kaman recorded 14 point-rebound double-doubles and led the team in rebounds in 16 games and in blocks 19 times. Despite the Clippers missing the playoffs again for the eighth year in a row, Kaman continued to show progress in his play. By the end of the '05–'06 season, Kaman averaged 11.9 points, 9.6 rebounds and 1.38 blocks in 32.8 minutes per game, appearing in 78 games (78 starts). He missed two games with a sprained left ankle (2/27 and March 1) and one game with a sore left knee (4/16) He finished the regular season ranked 9th in the NBA in rebounds per game (9.6), 12th in FG% (.523) and 24th in blocks per game (1.38). Kaman recorded 49 games of scoring in double figures with 10 of those games scoring 20 points or more. Kaman also recorded 36 games with 10 or more rebounds. Kaman finished the season with 29 games having points-rebounds double-doubles. The Clippers achieved their first winning record in 14 seasons and clinched their first playoff spot since 1997. By the end of the season, the Clippers finished sixth in the Western Conference, with a record of 47–35 (their best finish since the team left Buffalo), set to face the [[Denver Nuggets]] in the first round. The Clippers beat the Nuggets, but during the series against Denver, opposing player [[Reggie Evans]] reached in and yanked Kaman's [[testicles]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=2428627 |title=ESPN – Kaman: Evans pulled testicles, prompting outburst – NBA |publisher=[[ESPN]] |date=May 1, 2006 |access-date=August 3, 2012}} Evans was later fined $10,000 for his actions.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/playoffs2006/news/story?id=2429401 |title=ESPN – Evans fined $10,000, assessed flagrant foul – NBA |publisher=[[ESPN]] |date=May 1, 2006 |access-date=August 3, 2012}} The Clippers went on to lose to the Suns in the next round. [[File:Chris Kaman 2011.jpg|thumb|Kaman was named an [[NBA All-Star Game|NBA All-Star]] in [[2010 NBA All-Star Game|2010]].]] Kaman had raised his points and rebounds averages each season since he came into the league, and signed a five-year contract worth $52.5 million in October 2006.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=2641609 |title=ESPN – Kaman signs five-year extension with Clippers |publisher=[[ESPN]] |date=September 1, 2006 |access-date=August 3, 2012}} Thus 2006–2007, especially after a strong playoff run, was supposed to be a season of high expectations. However, Kaman only managed to average 10.1 points, 7.8 rebounds and 1.5 blocks in 29 minutes per game, appearing in 75 games. One possible explanation was that Kaman had been slowed down by a hamstring injury in training camp, limiting his mobility. This had resulted in a difficulty to get into a game rhythm and contribute offensively. The Clippers finished the season 40–42, missing the playoffs by one game. After losing [[Shaun Livingston]] and [[Elton Brand]] for the majority of the 2007–08 season due to a [[Joint dislocation|dislocated]] knee and ruptured [[Achilles tendon]], respectively, the Clippers had very little expectations to be as competitive as they were two years prior. However, Kaman emerged as one of the most dominant centers in the NBA, averaging 15.7 points, 12.7 rebounds, and 2.8 blocks per game. Although he did not play in enough games to qualify for the league's statistical leaders, his rebound and block averages would have both ranked third in the league. Kaman demonstrated his ability to perform without Brand alongside him. Kaman was selected to [[2010 NBA All-Star Game|his first All-Star Game]] as a reserve. Kaman finished the season with almost a double-double, averaging a career high 18.5 PPG and 9.3 RPG. Still, the Los Angeles Clippers finished with one of the worst records in the western conference, with a record of 29–53. ===New Orleans Hornets (2011–2012)=== On December 14, 2011, the Clippers traded Kaman, [[Al-Farouq Aminu]], [[Eric Gordon]] and a 2012 first-round pick (previously acquired from the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]]) to the [[New Orleans Hornets]] in exchange for [[Chris Paul]] and two future second-round picks.{{cite news|url=http://www.nba.com/hornets/news/hornets_clippers_trade_2011_12_14.html|title=HORNETS ACQUIRE GORDON, AMINU, KAMAN AND FIRST ROUND PICK | work=[[NBA.com]]|date=December 14, 2011 | access-date=December 15, 2011}} In his first ever game as a Hornet, Kaman recorded 10 points and 5 rebounds. Five days later he recorded a season-high 15 rebounds.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20120101/NOHSAC/gameinfo.html#nbaGIboxscore |title=FINAL |work=Nba.com |access-date=August 3, 2012}} On January 28, 2012, the Hornets announced that they were looking to trade Kaman, who was their oldest player at the time, to a contending team as they wanted to give more minutes to their younger players.{{cite web|author=Marc Stein |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/7511891/new-orleans-hornets-actively-shopping-c-chris-kaman |title=New Orleans Hornets actively shopping C Chris Kaman – ESPN |publisher=Espn.go.com |date=January 28, 2012 |access-date=August 3, 2012}} They deactivated him as they searched for a trade partner, but decided to bring him back to the team after a week of being unable to find a suitable deal.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/7538226/new-orleans-hornets-take-chris-kaman-trade-market-source-say |title=New Orleans Hornets take Chris Kaman off trade market, source say – ESPN |publisher=Espn.go.com |date=February 3, 2012 |access-date=August 3, 2012}} In his first game back, he played 22 minutes off the bench, and had 10 points and 12 rebounds against the Kings,{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20120206/SACNOH/gameinfo.html#nbaGIboxscore |title=FINAL |work=Nba.com |access-date=August 3, 2012}} and followed that performance up with a 17 points, nine rebounds outing against the Bulls in 30 minutes of action.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20120208/CHINOH/gameinfo.html#nbaGIboxscore |title=FINAL |work=Nba.com |access-date=August 3, 2012}} On February 14, 2012, Kaman scored 27 points and 13 rebounds in a win over the Utah Jazz, just ahead of the trade deadline.[http://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/id/320213003 Chris Kaman goes for 27 points, 13 rebounds as Hornets silence Jazz]{{dead link|date=July 2024|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}} Though observers speculated his recent performances would reopen trade discussions,{{Cite web | url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/1071188-nba-trade-rumors-best-destinations-for-hornets-chris-kaman | title=NBA Trade Rumors: Best Destinations for Hornets' Chris Kaman | website=[[Bleacher Report]] }}{{Cite web | url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/1090672-nba-trade-rumors-three-possible-trade-destinations-for-the-hornets-chris-kaman | title=NBA Trade Rumors: 3 Possible Trade Destinations for the Hornets' Chris Kaman | website=[[Bleacher Report]] }} New Orleans ultimately decided to keep Kaman for the rest of the season. ===Dallas Mavericks (2012–2013)=== [[File:Chris Kaman Mavs.jpg|thumb|left|Kaman while with the Mavericks.|220x220px]] In July 2012, Kaman signed with the [[Dallas Mavericks]], joining his former [[Germany national basketball team|Olympic]] teammate [[Dirk Nowitzki]]. Kaman and the Mavericks agreed on a one-year deal worth 8 million dollars.{{cite web |url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=10500 |title=Mavericks sign center Chris Kaman |publisher=Insidehoops.com |access-date=August 3, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131007062907/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=10500 |archive-date=October 7, 2013 |url-status=dead }} He would average 10.5 points and 5.6 rebounds per game in 20.7 minutes per game in 66 games,{{cite news|last=Bresnahan|first=Mike|work=Los Angeles Times|date=July 8, 2013|title=Chris Kaman agrees to one-year contract with Lakers|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/lakersnow/la-sp-ln-lakers-kaman-20130708,0,2022487.story}} starting 52 of them. The Mavericks finished 41–41 and missed the playoffs for the first time since the 1999–2000 season. ===Los Angeles Lakers (2013–2014)=== On July 12, 2013, Kaman signed a one-year deal with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].[http://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/130712chriskaman Lakers Sign Chris Kaman] He managed just 39 games for the Lakers because of a crowded frontcourt and a few maladies that started (food poisoning) and a (calf strain) which ended his season. He averaged 10.4 points and 5.9 rebounds per game.[https://www.espn.com/blog/los-angeles/lakers/post/_/id/39766/lakers-player-reviews-chris-kaman Lakers player reviews: Chris Kaman] ===Portland Trail Blazers (2014–2016)=== On July 10, 2014, Kaman signed with the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].[http://www.nba.com/blazers/news/trail-blazers-sign-center-chris-kaman Trail Blazers Sign Center Chris Kaman] Kaman appeared in 74 games for Portland his first season, remaining mostly healthy as the primary backup and occasional starter behind [[Robin Lopez]]. In his second season with the Trail Blazers, Kaman played in just 16 games, also logging minutes in Portland's first-round playoff victory over the Los Angeles Clippers. Kaman made his biggest impact in the locker room, and head coach [[Terry Stotts]] was complimentary of Kaman's veteran leadership.{{Cite web | url=http://www.nba.com/blazers/video/teams/blazers/2016/08/30/stotts | title=Stotts Talks Summer Progress on Courtside | website=[[NBA.com]] }} Kaman's final NBA game was played in Game 4 of the 2016 Western Conference First Round on April 25, 2016. In that game, the Trail Blazers would defeat the Clippers 98 – 84 with Kaman recording 1 rebound, 1 turnover and 2 fouls. ==National team career== Kaman played for the first time for the [[Germany national basketball team|German national basketball team]] in the [[FIBA World Olympic Qualifying Tournament for Men 2008|qualifying tournament]] leading up to the 2008 Beijing Olympics. In his debut with Germany, he posted a double-double with 10 points and 10 rebounds against [[Cape Verde national basketball team|Cape Verde]]. He was chosen the most valuable player by journalists.{{cite web |url=http://www.athens2008.fiba.com/pages/eng/fe/08/olymQual/men/news/lateNews/p/newsid/26673/FE_news_lateNews_arti.html |title=Kaman, Germans thump Cape Verde to reach quarter-final |publisher=Athens2008.fiba.com |access-date=August 3, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120213083618/http://www.athens2008.fiba.com/pages/eng/fe/08/olymQual/men/news/lateNews/p/newsid/26673/FE_news_lateNews_arti.html |archive-date=February 13, 2012 |url-status=dead }} Kaman rejoined the German national team for [[EuroBasket 2011]].{{cite news|url=http://www.basketball-bund.de/news/teams/a-herren/nowitzki-kaman-sagen-em-teilnahme-13471|title=Nowitzki und Kaman sagen EM-Teilnahme zu|date=July 22, 2011|access-date=July 22, 2011|publisher=German Basketball Association|language=de|trans-title=Nowitzki and Kaman will play the EuroBasket 2011|archive-date=December 21, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151221020703/http://www.basketball-bund.de/news/teams/a-herren/nowitzki-kaman-sagen-em-teilnahme-13471|url-status=dead}} ==Personal life== Kaman is a [[dual citizen]]; he is a citizen of the United States and of [[Germany]]. Although he did not speak any [[German language|German]] at the time, he acquired [[German citizenship]] in July 2008 (his great-grandparents were German), to play on the [[Germany national basketball team]] in the [[2008 Summer Olympics|2008 Beijing Olympics]].[http://latimesblogs.latimes.com/olympics_blog/2008/07/clippers-kaman.html Clippers' Kaman becomes German citizen for Olympics]. ''Los Angeles Times''. July 3, 2008. Kaman belongs to the Fellowship of Christian Athletes.{{cite web|title=Seven Minutes With Chris Kaman|url=http://www.fca.org/2013/10/29/seven-minutes-with-chris-kaman/#.U-_XthUo7IU}} On December 27, 2014, Kaman's wife, Emilie VilleMonte, gave birth to the couple's first child, a son named Barrett Christopher Kaman.[http://www.oregonlive.com/blazers/index.ssf/2014/12/trail_blazers_chris_kaman_on_birth_of_son_everythi.html Trail Blazers' Chris Kaman on birth of son: 'Everything in my life changes now'] Kaman started the YouTube channel "Exploring Kaman" where he and his friends go on fishing and hunting adventures.[https://www.youtube.com/user/ExploringKaman Exploring Kaman –YouTube] On July 13, 2024, Kaman played in a Gus Macker basketball tournament in Sault Ste. Marie, MI. ===Spokesman for diagnosis of ADHD=== In January 2008, Kaman revealed that he was misdiagnosed with [[Attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder]]{{cite news |url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/printedition/la-sp-cliprep14jan14,1,5750287.story?coll=la-headlines-pe-sports |title=Sea is choppy, but ship isn't sinking, Brand says – Los Angeles Times |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090301235654/http://www.latimes.com/sports/printedition/la-sp-cliprep14jan14%2C1%2C5750287.story?coll=la-headlines-pe-sports |archive-date=March 1, 2009 }} at age 2½. Kaman spent much of his childhood on a farm{{cite web|last=Washington |first=The |url=http://www.washtimes.com/sports/20060424-124323-9395r.htm |title=Washington Times – When Harry met the playoffs |work=Washtimes.com |date=April 24, 2006 |access-date=August 3, 2012}}{{cite web|url=http://www.spiegel.de/sport/ussports/0,1518,530262,00.html |title=NBA-Topcenter Kaman: "Habe schon darüber nachgedacht, für Deutschland zu spielen" – Sport – SPIEGEL ONLINE – Nachrichten |publisher=Spiegel.de |date=January 25, 2008 |access-date=August 3, 2012}} and as a child he used to tear shingles off neighbors' rooftops and misbehave in school. His apparent ADHD affected his play in high school, and he took [[Ritalin]] to treat the condition.[http://usatoday30.usatoday.com/sports/basketball/nba/clippers/2010-01-26-kaman-prospers_N.htm Of right mind, Clippers center Chris Kaman is prospering] ==NBA career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} ===Regular season=== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"| {{nbay|2003}} | style="text-align:left;"| [[2003–04 Los Angeles Clippers season|L.A.
